cps.title: CPS Test
cps.description: Tap as fast as you can across four timed intervals to measure your clicks per second. Includes 1s, 3s, 5s, and 10s phases.
cps.goal: Train hand-eye response, burst tapping speed, and short motor control.
cps.use: Best as a warm-up, quick break, or fatigue check.
cps.tip: Keep your wrist relaxed; compare averages across attempts, not just one peak score.

reaction.title: Reaction Test
reaction.description: Measure your response speed to visual signals. Tap as soon as you see green — don't tap on red.
reaction.instructions: Tap immediately when the screen turns green! Tapping too early incurs a penalty. 5 trials total, average reaction time is your final score.
reaction.goal: Train visual reaction speed and impulse control.
reaction.use: Best for a quick alertness check; sleep loss and stress often show up clearly.
reaction.tip: Relax while the screen is red. Tensing up can make early taps more likely.

tensec.title: 10-Second Challenge
tensec.description: Feel the passage of time in your mind and try to stop the timer at exactly 10 seconds. The more precise, the better!
tensec.instructions: The timer starts when you tap Start. Tap Stop when you think exactly 10 seconds have passed. The closer to 10.000s, the better your score!
tensec.goal: Train internal timing, rhythm sense, and steady attention.
tensec.use: Best for a quick attention reset before switching tasks.
tensec.tip: Do not count too forcefully; try estimating time through breath or body rhythm.

sbti.title: SBTI Personality Test
sbti.description: Discover your personality type through 20 quick questions. Find out which type you belong to!
sbti.instructions: Choose the option that best describes you. 20 questions total — honest answers give the best results!
sbti.goal: Reflect on your preferences, communication style, and decision tendencies.
sbti.use: Best for self-reflection, team icebreakers, or checking your current state.
sbti.tip: This is not a diagnosis. Answer by real tendencies rather than ideal answers.
sbti.q1: At a party, I tend to actively engage with many people rather than stick to a few close friends.
sbti.q2: I enjoy being the center of attention.
sbti.q3: I prefer talking through problems — discussing with others makes my thoughts clearer.
sbti.q4: I easily make new friends and socializing energizes me.
sbti.q5: Given the choice between quiet solitude and a lively gathering, I prefer the lively gathering.
sbti.q6: I focus more on concrete facts and details rather than abstract concepts and theories.
sbti.q7: I tend to follow proven methods rather than trying new approaches.
sbti.q8: I prefer dealing with practical matters rather than thinking about future possibilities.
sbti.q9: When given instructions, I like clear, step-by-step guidance.
sbti.q10: I trust experience more than intuition.
sbti.q11: When making decisions, I prioritize logic and fairness over personal feelings.
sbti.q12: I believe objective principles matter more than accommodating others' emotions.
sbti.q13: When criticizing others, I'm direct and don't worry much about hurting feelings.
sbti.q14: I prefer competition and efficiency in the workplace over harmony.
sbti.q15: I believe truth is more important than kindness.
sbti.q16: I like to make detailed plans in advance and follow them through.
sbti.q17: Having to change plans at the last minute makes me uncomfortable.
sbti.q18: Before starting a project, I want everything laid out and organized.
sbti.q19: I prefer a structured and routine lifestyle.
sbti.q20: Deadlines motivate me to get things done.

schulte.title: Schulte Table
schulte.description: Find numbers 1 through 25 in order on a 5x5 grid. Trains visual attention, peripheral vision, and reading speed.
schulte.instructions: Start from 1 and tap numbers in ascending order. The faster the better — mistakes add penalty time. Try using peripheral vision instead of scanning row by row!
schulte.goal: Train visual search, peripheral vision, and attention distribution.
schulte.use: Best before reading, studying, or starting focused work.
schulte.tip: Look near the center and use peripheral vision to find the next number.

stroop.title: Stroop Effect
stroop.description: Name the ink color, ignore the word! Trains selective attention and inhibitory control.
stroop.instructions: Ignore what the word says — select the color it's displayed in. Be fast and accurate! 20 trials.
stroop.goal: Train selective attention and inhibition of automatic responses.
stroop.use: Best before tasks that need calm judgment and fewer impulsive reactions.
stroop.tip: Attend to the color only. Slightly slower and accurate is usually steadier.

memory.title: Memory Match
memory.description: Flip cards to find matching pairs! Train your short-term memory and visual tracking.
memory.goal: Train short-term memory, position memory, and visual tracking.
memory.use: Best as a light mental warm-up or low-pressure training session.
memory.tip: Name the card and location after each flip; remember regions before details.

pomodoro.title: Pomodoro Timer
pomodoro.description: A work-break timer to help you sustain focus with a fixed rhythm.
pomodoro.goal: Train focus duration and a healthy work-rest cadence.
pomodoro.use: Best for tasks that need continuous effort, such as writing, studying, or coding.
pomodoro.tip: Pick one clear task before starting, and genuinely step away during breaks.

breathing.title: Breathing
breathing.description: Choose a rhythm for the goal: long-term regulation, pre-work focus, or quick bedtime downshift.
breathing.resonanceGoal: About 6 breaths per minute for autonomic regulation and HRV training.
breathing.resonanceUse: Best for daily maintenance: practice 10 minutes to support stress recovery and emotional steadiness.
breathing.resonanceNote: No breath holds, usually easier for beginners and breath-sensitive users
breathing.boxGoal: Equal inhale, hold, exhale, and hold cycles for calm focus.
breathing.boxUse: Best before work, meetings, or tests: practice 2 to 3 minutes to settle attention.
breathing.boxNote: Includes frequent holds, shorten pauses if it creates tightness
breathing.478Goal: Long-exhale rhythm to quickly lower arousal and relax.
breathing.478Use: Best before sleep, after waking at night, or during emotional spikes: 3 to 5 rounds is enough.
breathing.478Note: Shorten the hold or switch to resonance breathing if holding feels uncomfortable

frog.title: Frog Memory Leap
frog.description: Remember the frog's hop sequence across lily pads, then tap the pads in the same order! Sequences get longer each round.
frog.instructions: Watch the frog's path, memorize the order, then tap the lily pads to reproduce the sequence. The sequence grows longer with each level!
frog.goal: Train sequence memory, spatial path memory, and working memory span.
frog.use: Best when you want to stretch memory capacity until it feels slightly challenging.
frog.tip: Chunk the path into small groups instead of memorizing single pads one by one.

nback.title: Dual N-Back
nback.description: Monitor both visual positions and auditory letters simultaneously. Judge whether current stimuli match what occurred N steps ago. The classic working memory training task.
nback.goal: Train working memory, attention updating, and dual-task processing.
nback.use: Best for high-intensity training when you are already reasonably alert.
nback.tip: Start with a low N and increase only after your accuracy stabilizes.
